subject: EmberLake Dedicated: peaking projection & GPU slab runbook
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Asha Kapoor <asha@emberlake.ai>
Date: 2026-09-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated sizing kickoff — token profile and peaking expectations

Thanks Asha — good to connect yesterday. To get the Dedicated sizing right for EmberLake, please send the token profile (sample distribution: request sizes, percentiles, and any expected flash events).

Attached: emberlake_compute_request.xlsx (a tiny template that asks for historic qps/tokens, burst lengths, and typical sequence lengths). Key fields we need:
- Typical tokens per API call (median, p95)
- Expected sustained tokens/sec (daily peak and off-peak)
- Short spikes (duration and tokens/sec)
- Target p95 latency SLO for inference (ms)

If you can drop the CSV by EOD Tuesday we’ll run a model/SLOfit and propose a slab map (GPU count, SKU, headroom).

Best,
Laura
Laura Bennett
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Asha Kapoor <asha@emberlake.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@emberlake.ai
Date: 2026-09-14T12:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing kickoff — token profile and peaking expectations

Hi Laura, attaching our token profile (emberlake_token_profile.csv). High-level notes:
- Median tokens per call: 120; p95 tokens per call: 820
- Typical sustained traffic: ~6,000 tokens/sec during business hours
- Expected peak flash: ~18,000 tokens/sec for ~10-25 minutes during product events (weekly)
- Monthly avg token volume ~65M tokens; burstiness is our main risk
- Target p95 latency: <= 350ms for interactive endpoints; we can accept 500ms on lower-fidelity fallbacks

We also included an example request mix (chat vs embeddings) — chat is 78% of calls. Let us know if you need anything else.

Thanks,
Asha
Head of Platform, EmberLake

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-15T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: EmberLake token profile received — ask: slab mapping + SLO fit + headroom recommendation

Team — forwarding EmberLake profile. They have strong flash spikes (~18k tps for short windows) and want p95 <= 350ms. Can we do a quick runbook + compute mapping that covers:
1) Per-GPU sustained tokens/sec estimates (for candidate SKUs we support) at their median/p95 request sizes and with continuous batching enabled.
2) Peak slab sizing to hit 18k tps with a safety headroom target (recommendation: 30–40%). Include redundancy for a single-GPU failure.
3) Latency tradeoffs: if we need to hit 350ms p95, how many GPUs vs batching behavior vs smaller quantized model options?
4) Canary plan: what a two-week canary looks like (metrics, heatmaps, throttles, fallback rules).

Attachments: emberlake_compute_request.xlsx, emberlake_token_profile.csv

Karthik — can you take 1–3? Marcus — can you outline the canary infra and recovery playbook? Ben — I’ll need a quick commitment proposal (monthly reserved slabs + burst credits).

Laura

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-16T09:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: EmberLake token profile received — ask: slab mapping + SLO fit + headroom recommendation

Quick analysis (high-level, numbers rounded):
- Workload assumptions from their CSV: median seq ~120 tokens, p95 seq ~820, chat-heavy (78%).
- Candidate SKU performance (measured on our runtime prototype, continuous batching enabled):
  - H100-80GB (stock): ~7,200 tokens/sec per GPU (median mix) at p95 latency ~310ms
  - H100-80GB w/ aggressive batching: throughput up to ~10,800 tokens/sec per GPU but p95 moves toward ~420ms (batching latency tradeoff)
  - Next-gen L4-class (4-bit quant) variant (lower quality fallback): ~18,000 tokens/sec per GPU, p95 ~520ms (good for emergency degraded-mode)

Sizing math (target peak 18k tps, headroom 35%):
- Required capacity = 18,000 * 1.35 = 24,300 tps
- Using conservative per-GPU 7,200 tps -> 24,300 / 7,200 = 3.375 -> round up to 4 GPUs
- Add redundancy (N+1) -> recommend 5 GPUs reserved for production slab to meet SLOs during peaks.

Operational notes:
- If we prefer quieter p95 (<=350ms) keep batching conservative. That pushes us to 5 GPUs. If EmberLake accepts more batching latency occasionally, 4 GPUs can be justified with dynamic burst from shared pool.
- Canary: run a 2-week canary using 3 GPUs (to validate traffic shaping), route product-event spikes through canary only after we validate warm cache and KV prefix hit rates.
- Fallback plan: configure automatic model-variant fallback to the quantized L4-class with traffic shaping and notice of degraded quality to the product team. That buys more burst without immediate capacity purchases.

I’ll draft a slab-runbook with exact perf curves and expected tail-latency graphs.

Karthik
Staff Engineer, Inference Optimization

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-17T11:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: EmberLake token profile received — ask: slab mapping + SLO fit + headroom recommendation

Laura / team — based on Karthik’s conservative sizing (5 GPUs reserved), pricing sketch:
- Recommended commercial offer: 5x H100 Reserved Dedicated slab + 3x burst credits (shared pool) for short product events.
- Estimated list: ~$35k / H100 / month -> 5 GPUs = $175k/mo list. Expected commit discount: 20–30% for 12mo reserved -> effective ~$122k–140k/mo.
- Alternative: start with 4x reserved + 2x burst credits and convert to 5x after canary if we see heavy tailing; this reduces initial sticker by ~$35k/mo.

I'll prepare a one-page mutual action plan and a draft term-sheet (I’ll include a canary clause: 2-week canary; if SLOs met, commit converts to the reserved plan).

Ben
Senior Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Asha Kapoor <asha@emberlake.ai>, procurement@emberlake.ai
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-18T16:38:00-07:00
Subject: EmberLake next steps and agreed runbook highlights

Thanks everyone — summary & next actions:
- We recommend a conservative production slab: 5x H100 (reserved) to meet an 18k tps peak with ~35% headroom and N+1 redundancy given EmberLake p95 target <=350ms.
- Canary: 2-week canary on 3x H100 starting 2026-09-28 (metrics: token/sec heatmap, p95 latency, KV prefix hit, batch sizes, error rate). Marcus will own canary infra and rollback hooks.
- Fallback: L4-class quantized variant as an automated degraded-mode if sustained overload is detected; quality notice sent to EmberLake product.
- Commercial: Ben to send draft term-sheet with two options (4x start + burst vs 5x reserved).
- Action items:
  - EmberLake: confirm canary kickoff window (Asha) and provide final procurement contact.
  - Redwood Ops: Karthik draft slab-runbook and perf curves by 2026-09-22.
  - Ben: term-sheet to procurement by 2026-09-20.

Attachments included: draft_mop_runbook.md (placeholder with rollback steps), emberlake_compute_request.xlsx, emberlake_token_profile.csv

Laura
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
